terms.gloss: on the way back, on the return journey
terms.grammar: in with the ablative of reditus
evidence: Cic. Att. 6.2.6: Quīntīlem in reditū pōnere
terms.comment: Cicero planning his year in Cilicia: June in the province, July “on the way back”. Of someone walking home, Latin more often says it with the participle: domum rediēns. Of the way there, see on the way (inter viās).

terms.gloss: on the way home (literally “going back home”)
terms.grammar: present participle of redeō, agreeing with the subject
evidence: Val. Max. 8.1.damn.4: cum ā lūdīs domum rediēns turbā ēlīderētur
Cic. Att. 5.21.9: Quīntīlis … in itinere est per prōvinciam redeuntibus cōnsūmendus

terms.gloss: on the way back, while coming back
terms.grammar: in with the ablative of the gerund of redeō
evidence: Caes. BC 3.8: neque ūsae nocturnā aurā in redeundō offendērunt

phrases.english: We’ll buy bread on the way home.
We’ll call on Grandpa on the way back.

phrases.latin: cum ā lūdīs domum rediēns turbā ēlīderētur
phrases.english: when, on her way home from the games, she was being crushed by the crowd

phrases.latin: ibi cum Jūnium mēnsem cōnsūmpsissem …, Quīntīlem in reditū pōnere
phrases.english: when I had spent June there, to spend July on the way back

sources: Lewis & Short: reditus · Lewis & Short: redeo
